raw.assessment: The incumbent achieved intended course sets in 32/40 exports and a 17-minute handling median, missing both targets. A concrete limiting observation is the seven-minute median for 24 exports with unchanged assignments: scheduled CSV production already supports low effort in that subgroup. Six affected exports coincided with assignment changes and two with renames, suggesting investigation without establishing causation. No sampled cross-center rows supports only that sample; the course-split center was absent. Short runtime and slow replacement delivery do not reveal active handling costs.

openings.claim: Current instructor assignments or mutable course names may cause exporter and coordinator disagreement about the requested week’s course set.
openings.delta: Locate disagreement in export selection versus the intended-course reference before changing selection logic.
openings.prediction: If selection causes the problem, changing current assignments or names while holding the agreed historical course set constant will change inclusion. If references cause it, exports may remain consistent while coordinator expectations differ.
openings.probe: In fabricated staging fixtures, vary assignment timing and renames independently. Agree intended courses with consenting coordinators, then compare selections using stable identifiers where available. Include a course split and verify every exported row’s center ownership.
assumptions: Historical assignment data and stable identifiers may be unavailable.
Keep participants private, CSV schema unchanged and attendance entry available.
Bound diagnosis within six engineer-days and existing hosting.

openings.claim: Does replacement coordination consume active handling time, or mainly add elapsed waiting?
openings.delta: Distinguish the handling target from replacement latency; runtime cannot identify the dominant handling cost.
openings.prediction: If requests and follow-up dominate affected cases, active minutes will cluster there. If checking or importing dominates, shortening delivery alone will leave most handling work intact.
openings.probe: Use two short sessions per consenting coordinator to observe fabricated first-use and replacement workflows. Time checking, correction requests, follow-up, downloading and importing separately; record inactive waiting separately. Prioritize one bounded change for evaluation across the next 40 exports.
assumptions: Fabricated workflows support prioritization, not proof of production targets.
Use authorized workspaces, documented CSV and existing resources; attendance entry continues.
Share the six engineer-day budget with the first probe.

raw.assessment: Assignment changes and renames suggest selection problems, but their causes are unproven. Two mechanism combinations merit bounded tests; neither establishes delivery within six engineer-days or achievement of the next-40-export targets.

openings.claim: Combine requested-week membership resolution with stable course identity at a center-scoped course-ID manifest interface, then render the documented CSV. Temporal resolution could preserve membership through instructor changes while identity resolution preserves it through renames.
openings.delta: Either component alone may leave the other source of omission intact; together they could preserve a course that is reassigned and renamed during one week.
openings.prediction: On fabricated combined-change fixtures, both components recover the intended course set while either alone fails. Ambiguous splits require an explicit mapping rather than automatic inclusion.
openings.probe: Compare baseline, temporal-only, identity-only, and combined selectors on unchanged, reassigned, renamed, combined-change, and split fixtures. Verify exact course membership, center ownership, CSV import, and concurrent attendance writes; estimate implementation and hosting cost before adoption.
assumptions: Stable course identities and sufficient week-specific assignment evidence exist or can be captured within the budget.
Read-only export preparation can coexist with attendance entry.

openings.claim: Combine coordinator course/week confirmation with immediate authorized regeneration at a validated center-week request interface inside the private service.
openings.delta: Confirmation alone still leaves replacement delays; regeneration alone can repeat the wrong selection. Passing confirmed scope into regeneration could make one correction produce a usable file.
openings.prediction: Compared with either component alone, the combination reduces repeated requests and active handling when the confirmed scope is accurate; stale timetables may erase this advantage.
openings.probe: Use counterbalanced fabricated tasks with six coordinators across two sessions. Separately time checking, correction, downloading, importing, and waiting; compare intended sets with task answers. Reject foreign-center course IDs server-side and test regeneration during attendance entry.
assumptions: A small internal confirmation surface and rerun control fit six engineer-days and existing hosting.
The existing CSV renderer can accept validated explicit scope.

openings.claim: Requested-week membership plus stable course identity may prevent omissions; disagreement may instead originate in coordinator references.
openings.discriminator: Hold agreed historical scope constant; independently vary assignments and names. Compare baseline, temporal-only, identity-only and combined selectors, including combined changes.
openings.fit: Diagnosis preserves constraints; implementation feasibility uncertain.
openings.probe: Agree intended sets with coordinators; test unchanged, changed and split fixtures. Check exact membership, center ownership, CSV import and concurrent attendance writes; estimate cost.
openings.uncertainty: Associations are not causal proof. Historical evidence and stable IDs may be unavailable; splits require explicit mapping. Local timetables may be incomplete.

openings.claim: Course/week confirmation coupled to authorized regeneration may reduce repeated corrections when confirmed scope is accurate.
openings.discriminator: Compare the combination with each component alone; separate active handling from elapsed waiting. Faster delivery may leave checking/import effort unchanged.
openings.fit: Diagnostic sessions preserve constraints; confirmation UI and rerun feasibility uncertain.
openings.probe: Counterbalance fabricated first-use/replacement tasks with six coordinators over two sessions; time checking, correction requests, follow-up, download, import and waiting separately. Check intended sets, reject foreign-center IDs server-side and regenerate during attendance entry.
openings.uncertainty: Stale references may erase benefit; renderer acceptance of validated scope is unproven. Fabricated tasks cannot establish production outcomes.

post_distill.decision: Diagnose before selecting one bounded change. Share six engineer-days and existing hosting; retain private authorized processing, documented CSV and attendance entry. Validate next 40 exports: median handling <=12 minutes, intended sets >=95%, zero foreign-center records. Sampled isolation excludes the split center.
